messages.content: "Can you help me find four restaurants in New York that serve Italian food and cater to my dietary requirements of being vegan and gluten-free, and then find four more restaurants in Los Angeles that serve the same type of food and also cater to my dietary requirements?"

function.name: find_restaurants
function.description: Locate nearby restaurants based on location and food preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find four restaurants in New York that serve Italian food and cater to vegan and gluten-free dietary requirements, and then find four more restaurants in Los Angeles that serve the same type of food and also cater to the same dietary requirements.

We have a tool `find_restaurants` that can locate nearby restaurants based on location and food preferences. It accepts arguments: location (string), food_type (string), number (number), dietary_requirements? (string[]). The default for dietary_requirements is "None". We need to call this function twice: once for New York with Italian food, number=4, dietary_requirements=["vegan", "gluten-free"], and once for Los Angeles with Italian food, number=4, dietary_requirements=["vegan", "gluten-free"].

We should use the tool. The user didn't specify a particular city or address, just "New York" and "Los Angeles". So we can pass location="New York" and location="Los Angeles".

We need to call the function. We'll do two calls. We'll produce the function calls. Then we will wait for the tool response.
